review_comment: User input from $_GET parameters flows into a shell command without sufficient sanitization, creating a command injection vulnerability. The code uses escapeshellcmd() and escapeshellarg() but these are insufficient for preventing all injection vectors. An attacker could inject arbitrary commands through the 'scope', 'id', or other parameters. Remediation: Implement strict input validation with whitelisting for scope values and ensure all user inputs passed to shell_exec() are properly escaped or parameterized.
line_snippet: $return = shell_exec($command . " 2>&1 & ii=0 && while [ \"2\" -eq \"`ps -p $! | wc -l`\" ];do ii=$((ii+1)); if [ \$ii -gt ".($sec)."0 ]; then echo 'Intelmqctl timeout!';kill $!; break;fi; sleep 0.1; done");
